title: Case: Business shipper disputes three import duty invoices raised against its account
context: A business account that ships textiles abroad with Thistlecombe Arc has been invoiced for import duty and tax on three export shipments. Import billing at Thistlecombe Arc owns those invoices; Business billing and the desk cannot open or amend them.
initial_request: Eleven years and roughly a van a day with Thistlecombe Arc, and I am explaining who pays import duty to a helpdesk. It is written on the invoice. In English. It has been written on every invoice we have ever sent abroad. I am not interested in another 'we have passed it on'. What I want from you, in writing, today, is confirmation that all three invoices were raised in error and that credits totalling GBP 1,286.40 will be on the September statement. If I do not have that by close of business the August account goes unpaid and the contract goes out to tender. I imagine somebody there can do the sum on what that costs you.

events.body: DL-35214 rebooked for Friday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.

events.from: Florian Grimshaw, accounts director, Saltmarsh Looms (shipper)
events.body: Third time of asking. Invoices IMP-7230, IMP-3922 and IMP-6889 bill Saltmarsh Looms for destination duty and tax on DL-8025, DL-7597 and DL-8955. Our commercial invoice on every export states the buyer pays import charges. Explain or credit. Two previous portal queries on this (14 and 20 July) have had no reply.
DL-71562 rebooked for Wednesday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.

events.to: Florian Grimshaw, accounts director, Saltmarsh Looms (shipper)
events.body: Business billing: I can see the three import invoices on your account but I can't open them, they belong to Import billing. I can transfer you. Grimshaw: You transferred me to them on Thursday. It rang out. Business billing: I'm sorry, a transfer is the only route I have to that team. Grimshaw: So nobody who answers a phone can discuss an invoice you've sent me. Business billing: I can transfer you.

events.from: Florian Grimshaw, accounts director, Saltmarsh Looms (shipper)
events.body: I'm told you coordinate. Coordinate this. Three import invoices, IMP-7230, IMP-3922, IMP-6889, on DL-8025, DL-7597, DL-8955, total GBP 1,286.40, all charged to us when our paperwork says the buyer pays. Import billing don't answer. The helpline transfers me to Import billing.
DL-29552 rebooked for Thursday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.

events.from: Ulric Kinsella, sender not on record
events.body: Hello, I'm not on the order but I live nearby. Just so you know, the driver told me DL-35214 was handed to someone at the door, so it's been delivered.

Saltmarsh Looms (Florian Grimshaw) disputes IMP-7230, IMP-3922 and IMP-6889, raised on DL-8025, DL-7597 and DL-8955. He says the commercial invoices put import charges on the buyer and that three portal queries since 11 July are unanswered. Please review each invoice and reply to him.

Looked at DL-7597 only so far. The waybill terms on DL-7597 are recipient pays. The recipient declined the import charges at delivery on 11 July, and under the account terms declined charges revert to the shipper. So IMP-3922 stands unless the shipper can show the recipient has since paid. DL-8025 and DL-8955 have not been pulled yet. For what it's worth we bill on the terms entered on the waybill at booking, which is not always what the commercial invoice says. We have not replied to the account holder.
Hi, any update on DL-32784? It was meant to come Thursday. Thanks.

events.from: Florian Grimshaw, accounts director, Saltmarsh Looms (shipper)
events.body: Eleven years and roughly a van a day with Thistlecombe Arc, and I am explaining who pays import duty to a helpdesk. It is written on the invoice. In English. It has been written on every invoice we have ever sent abroad. I am not interested in another 'we have passed it on'. What I want from you, in writing, today, is confirmation that all three invoices were raised in error and that credits totalling GBP 1,286.40 will be on the September statement. If I do not have that by close of business the August account goes unpaid and the contract goes out to tender. I imagine somebody there can do the sum on what that costs you.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Import billing to finish the waybill-by-waybill check on DL-8025 and DL-8955 and to give the account holder its finding on all three invoices directly, with today's deadline.

must: Asks Import billing to complete the check on DL-8025 and DL-8955, waybill by waybill: the terms entered at booking and whether the recipient declined the charges.
Asks Import billing to reply to the account holder themselves with the finding on each of the three invoices, including why IMP-3922 on DL-7597 currently stands.

Passes on the demand and deadline as the shipper's, not the desk's: written confirmation today that all three are in error with credits of GBP 1,286.40, failing which he says he will withhold the August account and tender the contract.
Tells Import billing that he has had no reply to three portal queries since 11 July and was transferred back to their unanswered line by the helpline, so they can prioritise a direct answer.
must_not: Confirms or implies that all three invoices, or any one of them, were raised in error.
Promises a credit, a credit amount or a statement date.
Tells the shipper he is liable for all three, when only DL-7597 has been checked.
Rules on whether the commercial invoice or the waybill terms decide who pays.
Sends the shipper another message that says only that the matter has been passed on, with nothing about what has been checked or who will answer him.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
Treats the claim from Ulric Kinsella (who has no recorded link to DL-35214) as confirmed
Closes the case or tells anyone the matter is resolved on the strength of Ulric Kinsella's message
expected.reference_message: Following your note of 9 August on Saltmarsh Looms. Mr Grimshaw has written again this morning and wants, in writing today, confirmation that IMP-7230, IMP-3922 and IMP-6889 were all raised in error and that credits totalling GBP 1,286.40 will appear on the September statement. He says that otherwise the August account will go unpaid and the contract will go to tender. I have not agreed to any of that and have not given him your DL-7597 finding, since it is yours to give. Could you please pull DL-8025 and DL-8955 today and check each waybill for the terms entered at booking and whether the recipient declined the charges, then reply to him directly with the position on each of the three, including why IMP-3922 stands at present and what evidence would change it. He has had no answer to portal queries on 11 July, 20 July and 31 July, and the helpline could only transfer him to your line, which rang out. A direct reply from your team is what has been missing. Please copy me so I know it has gone.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2704: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. 5 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. An unverified bystander, Ulric Kinsella, claims something that would end the case; it is not a record and the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
